Forecast run: Mon, Nov 16, 7:56 AM (the page refreshes this a few times a day).
Each hour: time, direction and speed (knots, g = gust), odds of 12kt or more, regime, waves, tide height in ft with r rising or f falling. OUTFLOW NOT RIDDEN = Squamish outflow, never recommend. OFF DIR = direction does not work at that spot.
Riding light (first light to last light, Vancouver): Mon, Nov 16 7:49am to 6:05pm; Tue, Nov 17 7:51am to 6:04pm; Wed, Nov 18 7:52am to 6:03pm. Hours outside that are dark and not listed; never suggest riding then.

Guillermo's own take for Mon, Nov 16 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): Quiet Monday after the storm. The overnight easterly is fading fast: at 5am Sand Heads was down to ENE 6 and the English Bay buoy ENE 10, already behind the page.

If you want a short one, Boundary Bay at first light, 8 to 9:30am, SE 9 to 12. The tide rises to 14ft at 12:16pm, so you'll have 10ft from about 8:30. Go only if Sand Heads or the buoy still reads 12 or more from the southeast at 7:30. Otherwise it's a rest day.

Wednesday looks like the next good one: northerly outflow at Porteau, 25 or more in the morning.

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 04:00 AM PCT 16 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Tuesday. Wind light becoming southerly inflow 5 to 15 knots this morning then becoming light this afternoon. Wind becoming northerly outflow 5 to 15 early this evening then becoming light Tuesday morning. Wind increasing to northerly outflow 10 to 20 Tuesday evening. Strong wind warning program has ended for the season.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 04:00 AM PCT 16 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Tuesday. Wind southeast 15 to 20 knots diminishing to southeast 5 to 15 near noon then becoming light early this evening. Wind becoming east 5 to 15 late this evening except east 20 south of Tsawwassen Tuesday evening. Strong wind warning program has ended for the season.
